comment:
* This class represents member element of an annotation. * It consists of name and value, supplemented with element * definition information (such as declared type of element). *
The value may be one of the following types: *
    *
  • boxed primitive *
  • Class *
  • enum constant *
  • annotation (nested) *
  • one-dimensional array of the above *
  • Throwable *
* The last type is specific for this implementation; a Throwable value * means that the error occured during parsing or resolution of corresponding * class-data structures and throwing is delayed until the element * is requested for value. * * @see AnnotationFactory * * @author Alexey V. Varlamov, Serguei S. Zapreyev * @version $Revision$

variables.name: ERROR
variables.comment: * Tag description of a Throwable value type.

variables.name: ARRAY
variables.comment: * Tag description of an array value type.

variables.name: OTHER
variables.comment: * Tag description of all value types except arrays and Throwables.

variables.name: value
variables.comment: a primitive value is wrapped to the corresponding wrapper class

variables.name: elementType
variables.comment: no sense to serialize definition info as it can be changed arbitrarily

methods.name: protected AnnotationMember setDefinition(AnnotationMember copy)
methods.comment: * Fills in element's definition info and returns this.

methods.name: public String toString()
methods.comment: * Returns readable description of this annotation value.

methods.name: public boolean equals(Object obj)
methods.comment:
* Returns true if the specified object represents equal element * (equivalent name-value pair). *
A special case is the contained Throwable value; it is considered * transcendent so no other element would be equal. * @return true if passed object is equivalent element representation, * false otherwise * @see #equalArrayValue(Object) * @see java.lang.annotation.Annotation#equals(Object)

methods.name: public boolean equalArrayValue(Object otherValue)
methods.comment:
* Returns true if the contained value and a passed object are equal arrays,
     * false otherwise. Appropriate overloaded method of Arrays.equals()
     * is used for equality testing.
     * @see java.util.Arrays#equals(java.lang.Object[], java.lang.Object[])
     * @return true if the value is array and is equal to specified object,
     * false otherwise

methods.name: public int hashCode()
methods.comment:
* Computes hash code of this element. The formula is as follows: * (name.hashCode() * 127) ^ value.hashCode() *
If value is an array, one of overloaded Arrays.hashCode() * methods is used. * @return the hash code * @see java.util.Arrays#hashCode(java.lang.Object[]) * @see java.lang.annotation.Annotation#hashCode()

methods.name: public void rethrowError() throws Throwable
methods.comment: * Throws contained error (if any) with a renewed stack trace.

methods.name: public Object validateValue() throws Throwable
methods.comment:
* Validates contained value against its member definition * and if ok returns the value. * Otherwise, if the value type mismatches definition * or the value itself describes an error, * throws appropriate exception. *
Note, this method may return null if this element was constructed * with such value. * * @see #rethrowError() * @see #copyValue() * @return actual valid value or null if no value

methods.name: public Object copyValue() throws Throwable
methods.comment:
* Provides mutation-safe access to contained value. That is, caller is free
     * to modify the returned value, it will not affect the contained data value.
     * @return cloned value if it is mutable or the original immutable value
